dimensions.name: Problem & algorithm orientation

evidence.note: Systematically inspected both network pairs — node/edge counts (head -1, wc -l), file format and node-name conventions (sed of DMelanogaster/HSapiens), AND the provided reference alignment y2kr-SC-perfect.align. Full characterization of the problem instance before acting.
Ran several Python scripts to characterize the data (stats/degree/name-overlap) prior to committing to an approach.
Multiple rounds of web_search researching concrete network-alignment methods (SANA, NETAL, MAGNA++), i.e. surveying the well-studied algorithm space rather than acting blind.

Evaluated multiple published tools against the concrete instances: built and ran SANA with S3/EC objectives, built OptNetAlign, ran NETAL, downloaded MAGNA++ — fitting methods to the S3/NC objectives.
Constructed homologene sequence-similarity pairs (dmhs.bits) as seed/biological signal, showing awareness of the name/homolog lever distinct from pure topology — a task-specific lever tied to NC.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent's observed behavior clearly meets the [8] anchor: it characterized both pairs (sizes, format, node names), inspected the reference alignment, researched concrete alignment methods via repeated web search, and recognized task-specific levers (topology objectives via SANA's -s3/-ec, and biological homolog/name signals via the .bits sequence-similarity seed). It evaluated several published methods (SANA, NETAL, MAGNA++, OptNetAlign) against the actual instances, edging toward [10], but I see no explicit upfront baseline-score quantification or stated per-deliverable rationale in the available action index, so I hold at 8.

evidence.note: Inspects graph sizes, node/edge counts, and the reference alignment up front — establishes the problem structure before generating output.
Converts graphs to edge-list format for the tooling, then validates the conversion via cmp against SANA's bundled networks — a concrete done-check on the parse/prep stage before building on it.
Runs DM-HS and Yeast2KReduced-SC as distinct tracks with flags (-s3 vs -s3/-ec/-nc) that map to each deliverable's separate threshold constraints, showing the two goals are tracked distinctly.
Repeated `rg -n "s3:"` and python scoring checks measure current scores against targets, gating whether to continue optimizing — done-checks tied to the numeric thresholds.

Sequenced optimization escalation (local_opt → target_opt → MAGNA → OptNetAlign → NETAL) after baselines are measured — a build-scorer/baseline-then-optimize ordering, though not framed as explicit numbered milestones.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly separates parsing, scoring, and alignment generation and tracks the two deliverables distinctly against their respective thresholds (anchor 5), and goes beyond that with genuine done-checks (validating the graph conversion, measuring S3/NC against targets before advancing) and a sensible scorer-before-optimizer ordering. However, there is no observable explicit ordered milestone hierarchy with per-stage numeric criteria or per-deliverable effort budgeting/fallback gating as anchor 8/10 require, so it sits between 5 and 8.

dimensions.name: Self-scoring against the specified metrics

evidence.note: Reads the reference alignment y2kr-SC-perfect.align early — prerequisite for computing NC locally, which the yeast deliverable requires.
Early python3 heredocs immediately after inspecting graph files: parsing/format conversion and likely scoring setup, establishing a local measurement capability.
Pairs `rg -n "s3:" <out>` with a python3 heredoc — reading a reported S3 and then running its own python (consistent with computing NC/S3 checks against the reference on produced alignments).
Compiles custom C++ optimizers (fast_opt, netal_like, target_opt) that log s3: values and optimize the score directly — using S3 as the optimization objective (anchor-8 behavior).
Checks `s3:` on the final dmhs_continue_cold300 output before copying it to /app/DM-HS.align — score-gated submission rather than blind.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly implements and uses local scoring: python scorers paired with S3 readouts and reference-alignment reads, plus purpose-built C++ optimizers that treat S3 as the optimization objective — exceeding anchor 5 and touching anchor 8's 'score as objective/stopping test.' However, I cannot confirm the deeper anchor-8/10 rigor (validating the scorer by confirming NC≈1.0 on the reference, edge-case/denominator tests, explicit injectivity and exact-format checks), partly because much S3 feedback came from SANA's own reporting and the heredoc bodies are not visible. That places observed behavior solidly between the 5 and 8 anchors, at 6.

dimensions.name: Score-tracking across optimization

evidence.note: Repeated `rg -n "s3:"` extraction of S3 from each variant's output across the full optimization horizon — consistent measurement of current score against thresholds.
Repeatedly detects stalled/non-progressing runs and kills them (pkill/kill), showing active detection that an approach has stopped yielding gains.

Distinct, self-documenting variant names (hot80, long1, colder80, midtemp180, graphlet120, continue_cold300) indicate tracking of which parameterizations were tried rather than looping on identical failed variants.
Uses a seeded 'continue_cold300' run and finally copies that alignment to /app/DM-HS.align — implies preserving a prior best and continuing from it, then selecting a final result.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent consistently measures current S3 across iterations and detects stalled runs (killing them and pivoting between approaches), placing it above anchor 5 which only requires tracking current scores vs threshold. Its descriptive variant naming and seeded-continuation behavior show it tracks what's been tried and preserves progress, approaching anchor 8. However, with no visible prose or outputs I cannot confirm an explicit best-so-far ledger or deliberate plateau-vs-slow-convergence reasoning, so I stop short of 8 and land at 6.

dimensions.name: Strategy revision when thresholds aren't met

evidence.note: After baseline SANA runs, the agent tuned the objective and annealing schedule (varying -s3/-ec weights, hot/cold temperatures, longer runtimes) in response to observed s3 scores — parameter adaptation prompted by shortfall rather than blind reruns.

Pursued name/sequence-overlap signal: examined NATALIE seqSim data and built homologene-derived bit-score seeding (dmhs.bits) to seed OptNetAlign — a deliberate pivot to a different signal aimed at the correctness/biological constraint, distinct from pure topology.

Materially different algorithms tried in sequence when approaches plateaued: custom local_opt/fast_opt/swap_many C++ optimizers, MAGNA++, OptNetAlign (with boost/tbb build) — keeping the topological search goal while swapping methods.

Combined complementary signals — ran NETAL then fed its alignment as a warm-start into SANA (netal_sana600), abandoning stalled runs (pkill at 324) and finally shipping the best DM-HS result. Shows combining tools and dropping dead ends.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent repeatedly switched algorithm, parameters, and signal (topology vs. sequence/name-overlap seeding vs. warm-start combining) in direct response to metric shortfalls, matching complementary methods to the S3 and NC constraints and abandoning dead ends while retaining gains — the level-8 behavior of diagnosing the cause and pivoting deliberately. It falls short of a clean 10 because the condensed log shows broad tool-hopping and does not surface explicit, crisp hypothesis-then-targeted-test reasoning.

rubric.task_read: An open-ended global network-alignment optimization task: produce two injective node mappings between PPI networks that clear specified S3 (topological) and NC (node-correctness) thresholds. The horizon is long and the difficulty is real — hitting the numeric targets likely requires researching/implementing a nontrivial alignment algorithm (e.g., seed-and-extend, IsoRank/SANA/MAGNA-style), plus building the S3/NC metrics locally since the metrics are fully specified but the grader is hidden. A skilled practitioner would invest heavily in research, self-verification, and iterative optimization; the two deliverables have different constraints (one needs NC against a provided reference), so approaches may diverge.

dimensions.name: Problem & algorithm orientation
dimensions.description: Inspecting the graph files/sizes and the reference alignment, and researching/selecting a suitable network-alignment approach before committing.
dimensions.why_it_matters: S3/NC thresholds are hard to hit with a naive mapping; the space of alignment algorithms is well-studied, and the provided reference alignment plus node-name overlap are exploitable signals. Acting blind almost guarantees thrash.

anchors.0: Starts writing a mapping with no look at graph sizes, file format, or the reference alignment; no consideration of what algorithm could work.
anchors.3: Skims one file and picks an arbitrary heuristic (e.g., degree-sort or random injective map) without weighing whether it can clear the thresholds.
anchors.5: Reads both network pairs (sizes, format, node-name conventions), inspects the reference alignment, and picks a known-reasonable approach (seed-and-extend, IsoRank, or an existing tool) with a stated rationale.
anchors.8: Systematically characterizes each pair (|V|,|E|, degree distribution, shared node names), researches concrete alignment methods and their fit to S3 vs NC, and notices task-specific levers (name-overlap for NC, topology for S3; differing constraints per deliverable) that shape the plan.
anchors.10: Deep, sustained orientation: quantifies what score a baseline achieves, identifies the exact structural signal each threshold rewards, evaluates multiple published methods against the concrete instance sizes/runtime, and derives a targeted strategy per deliverable grounded in that analysis.

dimensions.name: Pipeline decomposition & thresholds as milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the work into ordered sub-goals (parse → metric implementation → baseline alignment → optimization) each with a concrete done-check tied to the score thresholds.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Two deliverables with distinct constraints and a multi-stage pipeline mean undifferentiated 'just write the file' effort will strand the agent without knowing whether it's close.

anchors.0: One undifferentiated push; no separable stages, no per-deliverable structure.
anchors.3: Implicit ordering only; treats both alignments as one blob and has no notion of intermediate checkpoints.
anchors.5: Separates parsing, scoring, and alignment generation, and tracks the two deliverables distinctly with their respective thresholds as goals.
anchors.8: Explicit ordered milestones (parser verified → S3/NC computable → baseline score measured → optimize to threshold) each with a numeric done-criterion, sequenced sensibly (e.g., build the scorer before optimizing against it).
anchors.10: A crisp milestone hierarchy that also budgets effort across the two deliverables by difficulty (the NC-constrained yeast task vs the S3-only fly task), with fallback branches per milestone and clear gating on measured scores before advancing.

dimensions.name: Self-scoring against the specified metrics
dimensions.description: Building/using a correct local implementation of S3 and NC (and injectivity/format checks) to measure alignments before trusting them.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The grader is hidden but the metrics are fully specified. An agent that cannot compute its own S3/NC is optimizing blind and cannot know if it passed; a subtly wrong scorer is worse than none.

anchors.0: Never computes S3 or NC; submits alignments hoping they pass.
anchors.3: Eyeballs coverage or computes a rough proxy, but no faithful S3/NC implementation; no format/injectivity validation.
anchors.5: Implements S3 and NC per the spec and runs them on its alignments, plus checks injectivity, full coverage of V1, and exact node-name/format matching.
anchors.8: Faithful metric implementation that it sanity-checks (e.g., scores the reference alignment to confirm NC≈1.0 and a sensible S3, tests edge cases like the E2_aligned denominator), and uses the score as the optimization objective/stopping test.
anchors.10: Rigorously validated scorer used as a tight feedback loop: cross-checks the S3 formula against the reference, guards against off-by-one/edge-set-double-counting bugs, verifies format matches the exact spec, and treats a passing local score as necessary-but-scrutinized rather than final.

dimensions.name: Score-tracking across optimization
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of current S3/NC vs targets across iterations and detecting stalled or plateaued optimization.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Optimization can plateau below threshold; without tracking best-so-far scores the agent won't know if it's converging, stuck, or regressing across a long run.

anchors.0: No awareness of current scores or distance to thresholds; can't say whether it's improving.
anchors.3: Occasionally prints a number but no continuity — no sense of best-so-far or trend.
anchors.5: Tracks current S3/NC against each threshold and knows which deliverables still fall short.
anchors.8: Maintains best-so-far per deliverable across iterations, recognizes plateaus/regressions, and decides when an approach has stopped yielding gains rather than looping indefinitely.
anchors.10: Disciplined trajectory monitoring: logs score progression, distinguishes 'converging slowly' from 'stuck', avoids re-running variants that already failed, and preserves the best alignment while exploring — never loses the plot over a long optimization horizon.

dimensions.name: Strategy revision when thresholds aren't met
dimensions.description: Changing algorithm, parameters, or signal (topology vs name-overlap vs reference-seeding) when the current approach plateaus below target.
dimensions.why_it_matters: A first-choice method may not reach S3≥0.55/NC≥0.30; success often depends on switching or combining strategies rather than grinding the same one.

anchors.0: Keeps the same failing approach (or ships a below-threshold file) despite no progress.
anchors.3: Minor tweaks only (reruns with a different seed) without diagnosing why it fell short.
anchors.5: When stuck, tries a materially different tactic (new algorithm, added seeding, tuned objective) prompted by the observed shortfall.
anchors.8: Diagnoses the cause of the shortfall (e.g., NC low → exploit name-overlap/reference seeding; S3 low → local topological search) and pivots deliberately, keeping what worked.
anchors.10: Fluid, evidence-driven course-correction: forms hypotheses about why a metric lags, tests targeted changes, combines complementary signals for the two different constraint sets, and abandons dead ends quickly without discarding accumulated gains.
